findings.text: Cross-file query reports whether the linear address range must remain at smallest page granularity to allow per-page protection changes.
Diagnostic entry reports the configured physical memory ceiling in megabytes, or a distinct none indication when no ceiling applies.
Hotplug eligibility query for a logical processor delegates to the registered per-processor operations hook when present and reports ineligible otherwise.

Forced small-page table policy is affirmative under allocation debugging, negative when large-block update support is available, and otherwise follows hardened data, deferred protection pool and realm execution modes.

Direct-map granularity requirement is active when any of hardened data mapping, allocation debugging, deferred protection pool readiness or realm execution is active, evaluated without reference to large-block update support.
Early boot mapping establishes a linear correspondence for a physical interval in the initial page tables using caller supplied protections and creation flags.

Conditional early pool setup reserves a fixed-size physically contiguous region and publishes it through non-executable small-page mappings that prohibit block and contiguous coalescing; reservation failure disables the early flag with an error diagnostic, and an alternate build offers the same operation as a no-op.

Early area descriptor records virtual base, corresponding physical base, total extent, mapping attributes and caller site; extent grows by one page unless guard suppression is requested, and misaligned base or extent is rejected as a programming error.

Kernel image is partitioned into five early area descriptors covering executable text, read-only data, init text, init data and writable data, with guard suppression applied to all but the final writable segment.

Identity table provides a read-only executable window for low-level entry code at the root table level, plus a conditional small read-write window for a coordination flag when linear-map splitting or a specific isolation mode requires cross-processor synchronization.
Panic-time diagnostic chain is installed once at boot and on notification emits kernel relocation offset, processor feature state and memory ceiling information before returning success.
Booting without firmware services while the address translation hardware was left enabled is treated as fatal and aborts initialization.
Synchronous signal frame pairs generic signal information with a full user context record.

User frame accounting structure tracks frame base and chaining link, allocated versus permitted total sizes, and individual displacements for each optional processor state extension plus a terminal displacement.
Parsed user context collection holds one descriptor per optional extension, each pairing a user pointer with its observed record length.
Deferred access state carries an optional overlay permission value whose presence is indicated by a validity mask supporting query and update operations that distinguish absent from present.

Overlay permission handling across signal delivery saves the current permission while opening all keys, installs a fixed initial permission for handler entry, and later reinstates the saved value only when one was recorded.
Largest permissible signal frame allocation is two hundred fifty six kilobytes.
Terminator record and extra-context header each occupy their structure size rounded up to sixteen byte alignment.
Presence indicator for the deferred overlay permission value occupies the lowest bit of the validity mask.
Guarded-stack capability for signal handling is derived by masking an address with a fixed capability mask.
User-space address for an extension record is obtained by adding its recorded displacement to the frame base.

Floating-point context exchange requires exact record size agreement; preservation synchronizes effective state and tags the record with magic and size, while restoration selects plain vector mode, clears streaming and vector flags, and refreshes hardware from the supplied registers.

Floating-point mode and overlay permission records use fixed-size tagged headers; overlay value on preservation comes from deferred state and on restoration is staged back into deferred state rather than written directly to hardware.

Scalable vector restoration requires the supplied length to match the current task length and the streaming flag to be consistent with available capabilities; streaming demands a payload while non-streaming may be payload-less and then delegates to plain vector handling, with allocation failures reported as resource exhaustion and an alternate build unconditionally rejecting.
Thread-local extension register is spilled and filled directly between hardware and a fixed-size tagged user record with exact size enforcement.

Matrix extension handling requires length agreement with current task state; an empty record disables the feature while a payload record requires successful backing allocation before enabling and copying register state.
Lookup-table extension depends on prior matrix enablement, uses a fixed single-register payload size, and rejects any differing register count or size.

Guarded-stack context preservation adjusts the reported pointer to account for a pending token when the feature is active; restoration rejects unknown modes and fresh activation, collapses any disabled configuration to zero, records the mode, and stages the supplied pointer for deferred validation.

User frame parsing enforces sixteen byte alignment of base and records, containment within the reserved area, zero-size terminator handling, single occurrence per extension type, per-extension capability gating, and silent skipping of the fault-status record.

Malformed layout, duplicate or unsupported extension records, length mismatches and failed user accesses are reported as invalid or fault errors, while backing allocation failures are reported as resource exhaustion.
Early area registration treats misaligned base or extent as a fatal programming error rather than rounding or truncating.
